children: Communication services
suffered a second consecutive week of record-breaking outflows following a post-earnings sell-off in Google
, spearheading widespread selling across U.S. equities, according to Bank of America Securities.

The flight from communication services marked the largest outflow in the sector's history—both in absolute terms and as a percentage of market cap—since its GICS classification in 2018, per BofA equity client flow data.
Technology stocks
also posted a third straight week of outflows, while industrials
extended their sell-off streak to 14 weeks.
Defying the broader downturn, consumer discretionary
pulled in the largest inflows, and energy
logged its third straight week of gains to lift its four-week average positive for the first time since early September, the note said.
The sector liquidations contributed to a third consecutive week of net U.S. equity outflows as the S&P 500

fell 0.6%, driven by across-the-board selling from hedge funds, institutional investors, and retail clients. Hedge funds fueled the drawdown with their steepest weekly outflows since mid-July, flipping their four-week average negative for the first time in three months.
Institutional selling normalized by market cap also surged to a nine-year October high, BofA noted, accelerated by seasonal tax-loss harvesting ahead of the October 31 mutual fund deadline.
Overall, clients offloaded $7.1B in single stocks while steering $2.4B into equity exchange-traded funds, favoring small-
and mid-cap
equities over large caps. ETF inflows were broad-based across value
, blend, and growth
styles and led by tech ETFs, with only real estate
and materials
recording ETF outflows.

title: Communication services purge leads 3rd straight week of market outflows: BofA
